ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: As shown in the figure, in the right trapezoid $ABCD$, $AB\parallel CD$, $AB\perp BC$, $AD=CD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, extend line $BE$ to intersect line segment $AD$ at point $F$. $\triangle AEF\sim \triangle BAF$, if $CD=3$, $AB=5$, find the length of $DF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $CD=3$ and $AB=5$,\\
Hence $AD=CD=3$,\\
Extend $BF$ to meet the extension of $CD$ at point G, as shown in the diagram:\\
In $\triangle ECG$ and $\triangle EAB$, we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ECG=\angle EAB \\
CE=AE \\
\angle CEG=\angle AEB
\end{array}\right.$,\\
Therefore, $\triangle ECG\cong \triangle EAB$ (ASA),\\
Hence $CG=AB=5$,\\
Thus $DG=CG-CD=2$,\\
Since $AB\parallel CD$,\\
$\triangle DFG\sim \triangle AFB$,\\
Hence $\frac{DF}{AF}=\frac{DG}{AB}$,\\
Thus $AB\cdot DF=DG\cdot AF$,\\
Hence $5DF=2\times (3-DF)$,\\
Therefore $DF=\boxed{\frac{6}{7}}$.

raw_record.original_question: In the right trapezoid $ABCD$, $AB\parallel CD$, $AB\perp BC$, $AD=CD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and line $BE$ is extended to intersect segment $AD$ at point $F$. Also, $\triangle AEF\sim \triangle BAF$. If $CD=3$ and $AB=5$, find the length of $DF$.
raw_record.answer: Let $CD=3$ and $AB=5$. Then $AD=CD=3$. Extend $BF$ to meet the extension of $CD$ at point $G$. In $\triangle ECG$ and $\triangle EAB$, we have $\angle ECG=\angle EAB$, $CE=AE$, and $\angle CEG=\angle AEB$. Therefore, $\triangle ECG\cong \triangle EAB$ (ASA), so $CG=AB=5$. Thus $DG=CG-CD=2$. Since $AB\parallel CD$, $\triangle DFG\sim \triangle AFB$. Hence $\frac{DF}{AF}=\frac{DG}{AB}$, so $AB\cdot DF=DG\cdot AF$. Thus $5DF=2\times(3-DF)$, and therefore $DF=\frac{6}{7}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and AB is the base horizontal line segment; C is directly above B, and BC is vertical; D is at the upper left, CD is the upper horizontal line segment, and CD is parallel to AB; F is located on the left oblique side AD; diagonal AC and line segment BF intersect at E, and from the figure it can be seen that B, E, F are collinear, with the order B-E-F. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, take A=(0,0), B=(5,0). Because BC is vertical and CD is horizontal, AB=5, CD=3, so C=(5,h), D=(2,h) can be set. From AD=CD=3, get AD^2=2^2+h^2=3^2, so h^2=5, h=sqrt(5). E is the midpoint of AC, therefore E=(5/2,h/2). Let F be on AD, set F=A+t(D-A)=(2t,ht), then AF=3t, DF=3-3t. On the other hand, F is also on line BE, parametrize BE: B+s(E-B)=(5-(5/2)s,(h/2)s). Make the two representations equal: from the y coordinate ht=(h/2)s, get s=2t; from the x coordinate 2t=5-(5/2)s, substituting s=2t gives 2t=5-5t, so 7t=5, t=5/7. Thus AF=3t=15/7, DF=3-15/7=6/7.
